title: Valorising Seaweed Biomass as Films and Fibres

biological_context.medium: citric acid demineralised aqueous sodium carbonate

section_1_1.heading: 1.1 Aims and objectives
section_1_1.verbatim_quote: The overarching aim of this project was to evaluate the potential of seaweed-derived alginate for sustainable fibre and film applications. The specific objectives were to: Extract alginate from Saccharina latissima using an environmentally benign process and determine yield. Characterise structural and molecular features of extracted alginate relative to commercial standards.

section_2_1.heading: 2.1 Phase 1: Extraction of Alginate
section_2_1.verbatim_quote: Dried seaweed (2.5 g) was immersed in 83 mL of 4% (w/v) citric acid and agitated overnight (16 h) at room temperature... The pre-treated biomass was then suspended in 40 mL of 2% (w/v) sodium carbonate and agitated overnight to extract alginate as sodium alginate... The extract was centrifuged (4500 rpm, 30 min, 25 °C) to remove insoluble debris. The supernatant, containing solubilised alginate, was precipitated by addition of chilled ethanol (2.5× solution volume, pre-cooled to –20 °C)... The extract was found to have an elevated pH (~12)... dilute HCl was carefully added dropwise to the supernatant following sodium carbonate extraction... Following the pH adjustment, 2.5 volumes of cold (-20oC) ethanol was added.

section_2_1_scaled.heading: 2.1 Phase 1: Scaled extraction (15 g scale)
section_2_1_scaled.verbatim_quote: In this case, 495 mL of 4% (w/v) citric acid was used for the pre-treatment, followed by 375 mL of 2% (w/v) sodium carbonate for the first extraction step. Due to the larger biomass volume, residual insoluble material retained significant alginate, so a second extraction was carried out by re-suspending the pellet in an additional 375 mL of sodium carbonate.

section_3_1.heading: 3.1 Yield analysis
section_3_1.verbatim_quote: In the initial 2.5 g seaweed sample there was 0.63 g of alginate was obtained at 7 pH so it had a yield of 25.2%, in the second extraction 0.65 g of alginate was obtained with a pH of 7 and for the 15 g extraction the yield was 4.96 g or 33% which are all around the range where the yield should be normally so these results were good to proceed with.

section_3_3.heading: 3.3 HPAEC results and TFA hydrolysis
section_3_3.verbatim_quote: The pH 7 extraction showed an M/G ratio more closely aligned with that of the commercial Sigma alginate, while the pH 12 extraction showed minor deviations... ManA/GuluA: P1 2.355, P2 2.369, P3 2.491, Sigma 2.440; Total Alginate %: P1 91.3%, P2 90.2%, P3 91.5%, Sigma 99.4%.

section_3_4.heading: 3.4 GPC results
section_3_4.verbatim_quote: Sigma alginate (S) exhibited a broad elution spanning 10.5–17.0 min, corresponding to molecular weights of ~54–69 kDa with a heterogeneous distribution (PDI up to 1.31). In contrast, the extracted alginate (P) showed earlier elution (~10.8–12.8 min), corresponding to higher molecular weight fractions of ~215–251 kDa with a narrower distribution (PDI 1.02–1.17).

section_3_5.heading: 3.5 Tensile test results (Fibres and Films)
section_3_5.verbatim_quote: Table 6 Shows the Young's modulus and the mean elongation at break of all the fibre samples: FPS Young's Modulus 0.4 MPa, Elongation 51.25%; FP1 Modulus 0.1 MPa, Elongation 27.48%; FP2 Modulus 0.1 MPa, Elongation 29.31%; FP4 (citric acid) Modulus 0.1 MPa, Elongation 43.09%... Film sample FPF Mean Young's Modulus 0.1 MPa, Elongation 1.72%; FPS Modulus 0.357 MPa, Elongation 2.04%.

section_4_1.heading: 4.1 Discussion: Extraction and yield
section_4_1.verbatim_quote: Alginate was successfully extracted from Saccharina latissima using a two-step chemical process involving citric acid pre-treatment followed by sodium carbonate solubilisation, with ethanol precipitation to recover the polymer. Initial small-scale extractions (2.5 g seaweed) yielded 0.63–0.65 g of alginate (approximately 25–26% yield), while the scaled 15 g extraction produced 4.96 g (33% yield)... Controlled neutralisation to approximately pH 7, achieved by gradual addition of dilute HCl following sodium carbonate treatment, preserved polymer integrity.
